correctness.rationale: Fock-state distribution and PGF normalized exactly; no-click probabilities and variance reconstructed from independent bin indicators. The strict log inequality includes the h=1/2 endpoint. A/B monotonic proof and cutoff inversion establish all quantifiers. A positive two-sided exponential bound pins the uniform m-optimized essential singularity; derivatives and endpoint constants were independently recalculated. Finite checker verifies 240 direct click distributions and 120 cutoffs, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The established Q_B witness, one-photon-added thermal example and all-order thermal Fock distribution are explicitly prior. New content is the m-uniform sharp thermal barrier, exact optimizing resource threshold, and provably essential vanishing of the supremum negative contrast. Primary full-text comparison did not identify the latter statements; independent priority remains an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: The 2012 general Q_B identity, 2018 general photon-added law and 2020 click table together give the unoptimized formula by standard substitution; the sharp all-m phase diagram is a concise algebraic refinement, while the optimized essential exponent requires an additional singular-limit argument.

An unlocated broader analytic treatment of all-order photon addition, detector cutoffs or singular contrast optimization may already imply some or all of the claim; no independent literature-priority audit was conducted.
No finite-data statistical significance or sample-complexity bound is proved; Q_B negativity is a population-level criterion.

value.rationale: The precise detector thermal barrier tells when photon addition cannot make a standard nonclassical optical witness negative, while the least usable addition order solves a natural discrete resource optimization. The singularity of the best achievable witness contrast quantifies an otherwise hidden limit of its operational sensitivity, though it does not yield a finite-sample power guarantee. This is a motivated nontrivial global classification, not merely a known one-photon example.
